final:
I checked all 25 review issues against the PR diff and the surrounding code, and wrote a verdict for each to `verdicts.json` in the run directory. No code was changed and no replies were posted. Ruby isn't installed here, so nothing was executed; the verdicts come from reading the code. That matters most for issue 12, below.

| Verdict | Count | IDs |
|---|---|---|
| VALID | 5 | 0, 1, 4, 5, 7 |
| PARTIALLY_VALID | 13 | 2, 3, 6, 8, 10, 11, 12, 15, 18, 20, 21, 23 |
| INVALID | 7 | 9, 13, 14, 16, 17, 19, 22 |
| STYLE_PREFERENCE | 1 | 24 |

**Should be fixed (actionable YES):**
- **#7:** The embed URL is placed unescaped inside a single-quoted `href`, and raw_html posts skip the sanitizer. A URL containing a `'` can break out of the attribute.
- **#6:** The RSS import path stores feed HTML completely unsanitized, so a script in the feed becomes stored XSS on the forum. The page-fetch path is safer because it limits tags and attributes.
- **#4:** `i.content.scrub` crashes when a feed item has no content element. That also breaks topic retrieval, because the retriever runs the feed poll inline.
- **#1:** The postMessage origin check is a substring match, so an origin like `https://forum.example.co` passes for `https://forum.example.com/`. The impact is limited to resizing the iframe.
- **#12:** `<%- end if %>` in `best.html.erb` is a real bug, but probably not a syntax error. Ruby likely reads it as `end if <next statement>`, which wraps the block in a bogus condition. I couldn't compile the template to confirm. The fix is `<%- end %>`.

**Rejected, with the main reason:**
- **#9:** `revise!` only returns false when the stored text already equals the new text, so updating the hash keeps things in sync.
- **#13, #14:** `topic_embeds` is a new table, Rails never re-runs a migration that has already been applied, and `force: true` is used throughout this repo.
- **#16:** The username setting defaults to an empty string, never nil.
- **#17:** `cook_method` is only ever set internally.
- **#19:** `be_true` is the standard matcher in RSpec 2.14, which this repo pins, and it's used 268 times.
- **#22:** Those lines already existed before this PR, and the `cooked` value is ignored anyway.

**Overstated:**
- **#3, #11:** The SSRF and URL-scheme claims are overstated. The feed URL is an admin-only setting, and user-supplied URLs must match the embeddable host. Switching `Kernel#open` to `URI.parse(url).open` is still cheap hardening.
- **#23:** The `Date.parse` issue is real, but that line already existed before this PR.
